suitability_reason: Only decided issue is the sec. 6651(a)(1) addition, decided on failure to prove reasonable cause (illness) for the undisputed late filings; deficiencies and 6662 penalties resolved by concession.

taxpayer.notes: Partner at law firm Gordon & Rees LLP in 2011-2013; left firm in 2015; placed on involuntary inactive status by California Bar in 2019 for illness. Joint returns filed each year.

adjustments: disallowed Schedule A medical/dental and miscellaneous deductions (2011-2013)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Sec. 6651(a)(1) additions (reasonable cause due to illness)
conceded: Petitioner conceded self-employed health insurance deductions for 2011 and 2012
Petitioner conceded Schedule A medical/dental and miscellaneous deductions for 2011-2013
Respondent conceded the sec. 6662(a) penalties for all years

findings_of_fact.fact: 2011: extension expired Oct. 15, 2012; joint return filed Feb. 13, 2013
findings_of_fact.snippet: The extension expired October 15, 2012. On February 13, 2013, he filed a joint federal income tax return for 2011.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2012: extension expired Oct. 15, 2013; joint return filed Dec. 4, 2013
findings_of_fact.snippet: That extension expired October 15, 2013. On December 4, 2013, he filed a joint federal income tax return for 2012.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2013: extension expired Oct. 15, 2014; joint return filed Nov. 19, 2014
findings_of_fact.snippet: The extension expired October 15, 2014. On November 19, 2014, he filed a joint federal income tax return for 2013.

findings_of_fact.fact: Illness determined by California Bar in 2019
findings_of_fact.snippet: In 2019 petitioner was found by the California Bar to have an illness requiring him to be placed on involuntary inactive status.

findings_of_fact.fact: No evidence introduced that the 2019 illness was reasonable cause for late 2011-2013 filings
findings_of_fact.snippet: any evidence into the record showing that his illness determined in 2019 could be reasonable cause for filing his 2011, 2012, and 2013 returns late

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for sec. 6651(a)(1) additions to tax for 2011, 2012, and 2013?
issues.holding: Liable for all three years: returns filed after extended due dates; no evidence that illness was reasonable cause
issues.computable_reason: Lateness is mechanical from dates, but the outcome turned on rejection of a reasonable-cause (illness) defense for lack of evidence

decision.text: Decision will be entered for petitioner with the respect to the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalties and for respondent with respect to the deficiencies and the section 6651(a)(1) additions to tax.
decision.summary: Deficiencies sustained (by concession); 6651(a)(1) additions sustained for 2011-2013; no 6662(a) penalties (conceded)

notes: No stipulation; record is unobjected exhibits (returns, transcripts, notice) plus testimony. Court declined to reopen record re criminal plea (fn. 3). Addition amounts are as determined in the notice; not recomputed by the court. All returns filed after extended due dates per sec. 6651(a)(1) (due date determined with regard to extensions).
